tags: why does my dog lick my feet
script: You sit down, kick off your shoes, and your dog heads straight for your feet. It might feel strange, but there are a few simple reasons. First, your feet are packed with scent. After a long day they carry sweat, salt and a mix of smells that dogs find fascinating, and licking is how they explore and taste the world. Second, licking is a social behavior. Puppies lick their mothers, and adult dogs lick the people they're close to as a sign of affection and bonding. Third, it can be attention seeking. If you ever laughed, talked or reacted when they did it, your dog learned that licking gets results. Licking can also be a calming habit for dogs that feel bored or a little anxious. Most of the time it's harmless, but skip it if you've put on lotion or any medicated cream, because those can upset a dog's stomach. If your dog licks constantly or can't seem to stop, check with your vet or a trainer. To reduce it, calmly move away, offer a chew toy instead, and reward them when they settle. Consistency teaches them quickly.
